relatedSnapshot.title: Tutorial cannot be turned off
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem

A tutorial overlay appears above important UI elements and cannot be turned off. This blocks or interferes with normal use of the page.

 <image> 

## Solution

Provide a reliable way for a user to fully disable the tutorial so it does not continue appearing over important elements once the user has turned it off.

## Scope

* Tutorial UI shown in the product interface
* A control that lets the user fully disable the tutorial
* Persistence of that preference for the user after the tutorial is turned off

## Saved model / behavior model

* The system should store tutorial enabled/disabled state per user.
* Once a user disables the tutorial, it should remain hidden for that user until explicitly re-enabled.
* A temporary dismiss-only behavior is not sufficient for this issue.

## Permissions / ownership

* Any user who sees the tutorial should be able to turn it off for their own account.
* The setting is per user, not workspace-wide.

## UX behavior

* The tutorial should not obscure primary interface elements once disabled.
* Turning the tutorial off should be straightforward and discoverable.
* After a user disables it, the tutorial should not reappear unexpectedly for that user.

## Acceptance criteria

* A user can fully disable the tutorial from the UI.
* After the tutorial is disabled, it no longer appears above important interface elements for that user.
* The disabled state persists across page reloads and future sessions for that user.
* The behavior is user-specific and does not affect other users.
* The implementation does not only dismiss the tutorial temporarily.

## Open questions or design follow-ups

* Where should the control live: close button, settings, or both?
* Should there be a way to re-enable the tutorial after disabling it?
* What should happen if tutorial content changes in the future: stay hidden or re-show?
* Does the tutorial need different behavior on mobile vs desktop?

## Outcome

Users can permanently turn off the tutorial for themselves so it no longer blocks or distracts from normal product use.

relatedSnapshot.title: Audit for remaining off-pipeline generation paths
relatedSnapshot.description:
**Sub-ticket 4 of 4 for** ENG-10034 **(Hardening 2). Independent — half-day survey; can run any time. May spawn follow-up tickets.**

## Goal

The scheduled-follow-up path was the known off-pipeline generator, but the fabrication arc teaches that ANY generation path not flowing through context-pack + KB-rules + copy-review will eventually produce the next hallucination incident. Find them all.

## Method

* Sweep for model-call sites producing user-visible outbound text in the AI SDR / outreach surface: grep for AI SDK `generateText`/`generateObject`/`streamText` usage and direct provider client usage outside `apps/web/lib/ai-sdr-v2/agents/*` + `prepareAgent`.
* Candidate paths to check explicitly:
  * Manual-reply assist / compose suggestions in the inbox UI (if any)
  * Closure/ghosted follow-up messages (the `followup-workflow.ts` closure branch — distinct from the deferred follow-up branch)
  * Deferred-followup date-confirmation replies (`workflow/steps/deferred-followup.ts`)
  * Anything in `apps/web/lib/services/thread-followup.ts` and the CRM sync side (`ai-crm-entity-create/*` writes prospect-visible fields?)
  * Playground paths that can leak into production behavior
* For each path found, record: what it generates, whether it uses generateContextPack, whether KB rules apply, whether copy-review gates it, and whether its prompt is DB-versioned.

## Deliverable

A findings table commented on this ticket + one spawned sub-ticket per off-pipeline path worth fixing (parent: ENG-10034), each scoped like ENG-10041 (move to agent system) or the context-pack routing ticket.

## Acceptance criteria

* Every model-call site producing outbound user-visible text is inventoried with its grounding status; gaps have tickets or documented justifications.
